title: Sanam Motlaghzadeh will defend her PhD thesis
content:
Sanam Motlaghzadeh will defend her doctoral thesis entitled "Terrestrial water storage retrieval using improved satellite orbit determination” on the 28th of August, 2026 at noon in Exactum CK112 (Pietari Kalmin katu 5, Helsinki). Her Opponent is professor emeritus Markku Poutanen from the National Land Survey of Finland and the Custos is professor Heikki Järvinen.

title: Helsingin yliopisto toteuttaa ensi vuonna käynnistyvän kansalaisuuskokeen sisällöt
content:
The University of Helsinki won the competitive tendering for Finnish universities on developing the citizenship test. The tendering was organised by the Finnish Immigration Service. Among the Nordic countries, Denmark and Norway already require a citizenship test, and Sweden is in the process of introducing one. Approximately half of the EU Member States require applicants to demonstrate civic knowledge through a citizenship test or other means.   

The Finnish citizenship test will be developed by a wide-ranging, multidisciplinary group of experts from the University of Helsinki in collaboration among several fields and faculties. Their work will be supported by a steering group of doctoral-level scholars.  

The University of Helsinki will not be involved in administering or organising the test. The Finnish Immigration Service will answer questions pertaining to the organisation of the test as well as any questions by citizenship applicants.

title: HELSUS and RESET are planning a series of Horizon Europe matchmaking sessions for 2027 calls
content:
HELSUS and RESET are planning a series of matchmaking sessions in September–October 2026 to support consortium building for selected upcoming Horizon Europe calls. To help us identify the most relevant opportunities and participants, we invite expressions of interest via the Lyyti form below.

We are particularly keen to hear not only from colleagues in the natural and technical sciences, but also from researchers working in the social sciences and humanities, as well as from those with expertise in, e.g., policy, governance, law, economics, education, business, innovation, communication, and stakeholder engagement. Several of the calls explicitly require interdisciplinary approaches and, in some cases, the effective contribution of SSH disciplines.

If you are already involved in a consortium led by the University of Helsinki for any of these calls, please let us know. This will help us coordinate efforts and avoid unnecessary overlap within the university.

Deadline for expressions of interest: 14 August 2026 (Fri)

title: Genetic discoveries may help patients find the right blood pressure medication faster
content:
A large international study led by FIMM researchers has identified genetic factors that influence how people tolerate common blood pressure medications. The study highlights how genetic variants enriched in the Finnish population can reveal biological insights that may remain hidden in larger but more genetically diverse populations.  

High blood pressure affects more than a billion people worldwide and is one of the leading causes of heart disease and stroke. While several effective medications are available, many patients struggle to find a treatment that suits them. Up to half of patients stop or switch their blood pressure medication within the first year. 

To understand why some patients tolerate these medications better than others, researchers analysed genetic and health data from more than 400,000 blood pressure medication users in , the UK Biobank and the Estonian Biobank. 

One of the study’s most striking findings was a genetic variant in a gene called NTSR1 that protects against the persistent dry cough often caused by ACE inhibitors. The variant is found in around 3% of Finns but is extremely rare in most other populations.

title: Project researcher interviewed by Swedish Newspaper Hufvudstadsbladet
content: Madagascar has a contenious history in relation to land ownership. The Tozzi Green project is run by an Italian company and co-financed by FinnFund and a development fund from Belgium. Currently, the project is planting trees in support of being able to sell carbon credits in the global market. However, there is controversy due to the local population, particularly cattle herders, feeling that the land on which the planting is taking place is not appropriate for the Malagasy government to lease for these purposes. There are accusations of land grabbing in addition to the feeling that some of the ambitious promises Tozzi Green made when they came to the area have not come to fruition. Jenni contributes to the article by highlighting that this situation is illustrative of the types of conflicts of interest that can arise when the focus of development work shifts from traditional aid work to investment support for companies. In the Tozzi Green case the partners are not civil society organizations, but rather companies whose ultimate goals are to generate profit.

title: Metsäojitukset ja majavatulvikot muokkaavat samaa maisemaa vastakkaisiin suuntiin
content:
Boreal forests and peatlands are shaped by hydrological changes caused by both human activity and natural processes. In a recent study carried out in the Evo area in southern Finland, researchers examined how forestry drainage and beaver-induced flooding have transformed the landscape over the past 60 years. They combined historical maps, aerial imagery from different decades, current geospatial data and long-term field observations.

The study showed that between 1963 and 2023, the ditch network almost quadrupled in size and the proportion of drained peatlands increased from 23.8% to 72.5%. The substantial expansion of the ditch network reflects a long-term shift towards drier conditions.

The study also assessed, for the first time, the total extent of areas flooded by beavers in the Evo area. Altogether, 77 active and previously flooded sites form a wetland mosaic covering approximately 1.4 square kilometres. At the landscape level, drainage is clearly a more extensive hydrological change than beaver activity; locally, however, beavers create new wetlands and re-establish wetter conditions, particularly along the edges of bodies of water.

title: Kesän puutarhaopastukset Kaisaniemessä
content:
On a guided tour, you’ll journey through millions of years of evolution along the paths of the Evolution Garden, and immerse yourself in a world of scents and colours in the Garden of the senses. You’ll also admire unique lichen and moss gardens, while hearing stories about the garden’s past and present, and the buildings found in the area.

Tours will take place from June 23 to August 22, 2026. Free entrance, no prior registration required.

title: “Ilman pölyttäjiä maailma olisi ankea ja väritön” – Uusi näyttely avaa oven pölyttäjien kiehtovaan elämään
content:
Pollinators represent an astonishingly diverse group of animals, many of which possess remarkable abilities despite their small size. Bees can count, bumblebees solve problems, and on distant islands, even lizards can pollinate flowers.

The  exhibition, which combines science and art, offers a wealth of information, stunning visuals, and fun activities for visitors of all ages. Guests can play interactive games like "Identify the Pollinators" and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the museum's impressive collection of specimens. The exhibition is based on a newly illustrated non-fiction book.

– We want to show the world through the eyes of pollinators, says exhibition scriptwriter Mia Rönkä, Adjunct Professor in Environmental Ecology at the University of Turku. Rönkä has written the exhibition’s informational texts and poems.

Although the sensory perceptions, cognitive abilities, and communication methods of pollinators like bees differ from ours as humans, we can still strive to understand and appreciate them as individuals of other species – without anthropomorphizing them, Rönkä explains.

title: Arkadiankadun siltaremontti aiheuttaa muutoksia liikennejärjestelyihin Luonnontieteellisen museon lähistöllä
content:
The renovation will start with the construction of temporary traffic arrangements from Wednesday 7 January onwards. The renovation is expected to be completed in late 2026.

A temporary bridge for pedestrians will be built on the east side of Arkadiankatu over the Baana. The aim is to maintain the pedestrian route on the east side of the bridge until the temporary bridge is operational. Cyclists will also be able to use the bridge.

The Baana route underneath the bridge is expected to remain open for most of the renovation's duration, with some minor exceptions.

There will be changes to the motor vehicle routes by the bridge and around it in January. If possible, should be favoured during the bridge renovation.

Connections to the bus terminals in Kamppi will remain available, but there will be a slight diversion of routes.

Trams 1 and 1T will run via Simonkatu and Kamppi. Lasipalatsi and the Natural History Museum will not be served.

The diversion is due to the renovation of the Arkadiankatu bridge and will remain in place until late 2026. The renovation will not affect HSL's bus services.

title: Ukrainan sota - yliopiston suositukset
content:
The University of Helsinki has condemned the military action by Russia and expressed its support for Ukraine and its university community. We have also expressed our support for Ukraine, together with other Finnish universities, through statements by and the . As a demonstration of support, we have illuminated buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag and raised the flag on our premises.

One of the principles of the University of Helsinki is to promote international collaboration in research and higher education, and to support these efforts even in difficult circumstances. Russia’s indefensible military aggression in Ukraine has required exceptional measures, which include those taken in the collaboration between universities.

The University of Helsinki is monitoring both national and EU-level sanctions, adapting our policies and processes accordingly. Together with other Finnish and international universities, the University of Helsinki strives to promote the end of military action in Ukraine, while supporting Ukrainian institutions and people.

title: Una Europa -verkostolle myönnettiin rahoitus vuosiksi 2026–2028
content:
Una Europa is a network of European universities established in 2018 to strengthen the European university landscape, and the University of Helsinki has been a member since 2019.  Una Europa aims to offer new opportunities for study, mobility, and academic collaboration to staff and students of the member universities. 

Launching in November 2026, the Una.Via project will strengthen sustainable international cooperation among the universities. The project builds on the successes of previous pilot projects and focuses on practical actions. Its key objectives include establishing new Interdisciplinary Hubs to support teaching and research collaboration, developing training academy to advance the skills of staff and students, and strengthening the role of students as co-creators. 

The University of Helsinki plays a key role in the Una.Via project, taking the lead responsibility for creating new collaborative structures. UH’s key tasks include developing the Interdisciplinary Hubs, coordinating their supporting specialist groups, and launching a new funding instrument for new research and education initiatives.
